strings.name: Shirin Neshat
strings.summary: Born in Iran, Shirin Neshat went to the United States as a young woman to study art. Through photography, video installations and film she has explored women, power and exile. Works such as Women of Allah combine portraits and Persian writing, drawing international attention to tensions around gender, religion and identity. She received the International Award at the 1999 Venice Art Biennale and the Silver Lion for best director at the 2009 Venice Film Festival for Women Without Men, continuing to work across cultures thereafter.

strings.influence.rationale: Through photography, video and film, she explores Iranian women, power and the experience of exile, advancing the expression of Middle Eastern culture in international art.

strings.highlights.women.title: Visual expression of women and power
strings.highlights.women.text: Women of Allah combines women’s portraits and Persian writing to explore gender, religion and politics after Iran’s revolution.
strings.highlights.venice.title: Across art and cinema
strings.highlights.venice.text: She received the 1999 Venice Art Biennale International Award and the 2009 Venice Film Festival Silver Lion for best director, honours from separate events.
strings.timeline.trilogy26.title: New work on immigration and America
strings.timeline.trilogy26.text: She presented the trilogy Do U Dare! in Venice and discussed Iranian immigrants’ loneliness and identity in America in an interview that year.
strings.timeline.broad19.title: Retrospective in Los Angeles
strings.timeline.broad19.text: The Broad presented I Will Greet the Sun Again, surveying her photographs and video installations and introducing Land of Dreams.
strings.timeline.prize17.title: Praemium Imperiale
strings.timeline.prize17.text: She received the painting award; the organiser recognised her work across photography, video installations and film.
strings.timeline.film09.title: Silver Lion for film directing
strings.timeline.film09.text: Her first feature, Women Without Men, won the Venice Film Festival’s Silver Lion for best director, extending her art practice into narrative cinema.
strings.timeline.biennale99.title: Venice Art Biennale award
strings.timeline.biennale99.text: Her video work, including Turbulent and Rapture, received the International Award at the 48th Venice Art Biennale.
strings.timeline.women93.title: Began Women of Allah
strings.timeline.women93.text: From 1993 to 1997 she used women’s portraits, Persian writing and symbolic objects to examine power and gender in Iranian society.
strings.timeline.return90.title: A turning point on returning to Iran
strings.timeline.return90.text: After years in the United States she revisited Iran and observed post-revolutionary changes, an experience that informed her subsequent work centred on women.
strings.timeline.study74.title: Moved to the United States to study
strings.timeline.study74.text: She left Iran for the United States at 17 and later studied art at the University of California, Berkeley.
